agenda: The situation in the Middle East; Letter dated 15 October 2025 from the Panel of Experts on Yemen addressed to the President of the Security Council (S/2025/650)
penholder: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
steps.intent: The United Kingdom's primary objective as penholder is to secure the routine 12-month renewal of the targeted sanctions regime (asset freeze and travel ban) and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, preserving essential oversight of arms embargo violations and illicit financial flows. The main negotiating friction points will be demands from the Russian Federation and China to avoid controversial language addressing regional maritime tensions or overly broad political condemnations, alongside the necessity of retaining Council unity on demanding the release of detained UN and humanitarian personnel. By focusing the text strictly on the mandate rollover and established humanitarian safeguards, the UK aims to achieve consensus and maintain the Council's 15-0-0 track record on this file.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the renewal of the sanctions measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts to maintain stability and prevent further escalation. We believe the draft must clearly underscore that only an inclusive, Yemeni-led political process under UN auspices can achieve lasting peace, while ensuring that sanctions do not compound the severe economic and humanitarian suffering of Yemeni civilians. We look forward to working constructively with the penholder to finalize the text.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of the Yemen sanctions regime and the extension of the mandate of the Panel of Experts as a constructive measure to maintain regional stability. We emphasize that sanctions are a means, not an end, and must serve the overarching objective of reaching a comprehensive political settlement. We appreciate the penholder's efforts to present a concise text and propose these modest additions to reflect the Council's consistent support for dialogue and the UN-led political track.
messages.Denmark: Denmark strongly supports the UK-led draft to renew the Yemen sanctions measures and extend the Panel of Experts' mandate, whose independent reporting is vital. As a major seafaring nation, Denmark views the continued attacks on maritime navigation in the Red Sea as unacceptable and believes the text should explicitly reflect Council resolution 2722 (2024) on the protection of maritime rights and merchant shipping. We also welcome the strong call for the unconditional release of detained United Nations and humanitarian staff, and we stand ready to support swift adoption.
messages.France: France thanks the United Kingdom for circulating this timely and balanced draft resolution renewing the 2140 sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts. We particularly welcome the firm condemnation and demand for the immediate, unconditional release of detained United Nations, humanitarian, and diplomatic personnel, as well as the continued vigilance regarding illicit arms transfers. France fully supports this text as drafted and urges the Council to adopt it swiftly to maintain unity and preserve vital monitoring mechanisms.
messages.Greece: Greece welcomes the draft circulated by the United Kingdom and fully supports the extension of the sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts. As a leading maritime nation, Greece believes the Council must clearly reaffirm the imperative of safeguarding navigational rights and freedoms and condemning attacks against commercial shipping in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, in accordance with international law and resolution 2722 (2024). We stand ready to engage constructively with the penholder and Council colleagues to finalize the resolution.
messages.Guyana: Guyana thanks the United Kingdom for circulating this timely draft renewing the 2140 sanctions measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts. We welcome the emphasis on safeguarding humanitarian assistance and the urgent call for the unconditional release of detained United Nations and NGO personnel. We believe the resolution would be further strengthened by reaffirming the Council's support for the Special Envoy and the UN-led political process aimed at achieving a sustainable and peaceful settlement.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the draft resolution renewing the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, which remain important instruments for supporting stability and security in Yemen. We believe the text would benefit from a concise reaffirmation of Council support for the UN-led political process and ongoing regional mediation efforts towards a peaceful resolution of the conflict. Pakistan remains committed to working constructively with the penholder and all Council members to achieve consensus on this renewal.
messages.Panama: Panama thanks the United Kingdom for preparing this draft and strongly supports the renewal of the sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts on Yemen. Given our role as a major flag state and proponent of international commerce, we would appreciate the inclusion of language reaffirming maritime security and the safety of commercial shipping in the Red Sea. We remain fully committed to supporting the adoption of this resolution.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea thanks the United Kingdom for preparing a concise and well-balanced draft resolution extending the 2140 sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts. As Chair of the 2140 Sanctions Committee, we attach paramount importance to preserving Council unity and ensuring the uninterrupted, effective functioning of the sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts. We fully support the draft as tabled, including its clear demand for the immediate release of detained United Nations and humanitarian personnel, and look forward to its unanimous adoption.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports maintaining the unity of the Security Council on the Yemen sanctions file through an unencumbered technical rollover of the measures and the Panel's mandate. We must avoid importing contentious, non-consensus elements from outside the 2140 sanctions framework, specifically resolution 2722 (2024). We ask the penholder to delete the reference to resolution 2722 (2024) in PP1 to preserve the purely technical character of the text.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the draft resolution renewing the targeted sanctions measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts on Yemen. We particularly welcome the explicit language demanding the immediate and unconditional release of detained United Nations and humanitarian personnel, as well as the protection of humanitarian operations. We propose a modest addition reaffirming Council support for the Special Envoy's political efforts to ensure momentum toward a durable political settlement is sustained.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks the United Kingdom for circulating this timely and balanced draft resolution renewing the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts on Yemen. We particularly welcome the explicit inclusion of language demanding the immediate, safe, and unconditional release of arbitrarily detained United Nations, NGO, and diplomatic personnel. Maintaining the Council's unity on this file is crucial, and Slovenia stands ready to support the adoption of this text as drafted.
messages.Somalia: Somalia welcomes the United Kingdom’s draft resolution renewing the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts on Yemen, both of which remain critical to regional stability. As an immediate coastal neighbor directly impacted by maritime weapons smuggling networks that cross the Gulf of Aden to supply terrorist networks such as Al-Shabaab and Da'esh affiliates, we believe enhanced collaboration between the Yemen Panel and the Panel of Experts on Somalia is essential. We appreciate the penholder's efforts and look forward to working constructively toward an early adoption.
messages.United States of America: The United States strongly supports the extension of the Yemen sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, which remain critical tools to counter destabilizing activities and disrupt illicit arms flows. We appreciate the United Kingdom's stewardship as penholder and believe the text must clearly reflect the severe and continued threat posed by Houthi attacks against commercial shipping and maritime security. We look forward to working constructively with the penholder and Council colleagues to swiftly achieve a strong, unanimous adoption.

The draft smoothly renews the targeted sanctions regime under resolution 2140 and the mandate of the Panel of Experts for 12 months, while addressing maritime security, arms embargo enforcement, the release of detained UN personnel, and support for the political process.

after.Denmark:
Mr. President,

I wish to thank the penholder, the United Kingdom, for its efforts leading to the unanimous adoption of this resolution.

Denmark voted in favour of the resolution. We welcome the extension of the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts. The independent reporting of the Panel remains vital to monitoring violations of the targeted arms embargo and supporting the work of this Council.

As a major maritime nation, Denmark remains deeply committed to maritime security, the safety of seafarers, and the exercise of navigational rights and freedoms in accordance with international law. Attacks against commercial and merchant vessels in the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden threaten international commerce and regional stability, and they must cease immediately.

We also reiterate our profound concern over the arbitrary detention by the Houthis of United Nations personnel, staff of international and non-governmental organisations, and diplomatic staff. We demand their immediate, safe, and unconditional release. 

Finally, Denmark reiterates that there is no military solution to the conflict in Yemen. We reaffirm our full support for the Special Envoy of the Secretary-General and call on all parties to engage constructively in an inclusive, Yemeni-led and Yemeni-owned political process under United Nations auspices to achieve a lasting and sustainable peace.

I thank you.
after.Greece:
I would like to thank the United Kingdom, as penholder, for its efforts in facilitating the unanimous adoption of this resolution.

Greece voted in favour of the resolution renewing the sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts on Yemen. We consider the 2140 sanctions framework and the targeted arms embargo established pursuant to resolution 2216 (2015) essential instruments for deterring destabilising activities, preventing the illicit transfer of weapons, and supporting the broader efforts to achieve lasting peace and security in Yemen and the region.

As a leading maritime nation, Greece attaches paramount importance to maritime security, the safety of seafarers, and the preservation of freedom of navigation in accordance with international law, in particular the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). The persistent attacks against commercial and merchant vessels in the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden represent a grave threat to international navigation, global trade, and the marine environment, and they must cease immediately. We also reiterate our serious concern over the continued illicit flow of arms and advanced weaponry, which directly fuels these reckless attacks and exacerbates the conflict.

At the same time, we remain deeply concerned by the dire humanitarian situation facing the Yemeni people. Full, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access must be ensured, and civilian suffering must not be compounded. We also reiterate our call for the immediate, safe, and unconditional release of all detained United Nations, non-governmental organisation, and diplomatic personnel.

In conclusion, there can be no military solution to the conflict in Yemen. Greece reaffirms its steadfast support for the Special Envoy of the Secretary-General, Hans Grundberg, and his tireless efforts to achieve an inclusive, Yemeni-led and Yemeni-owned political transition under United Nations auspices, restoring long-overdue peace and stability to Yemen and the wider region.

I thank you.
after.Guyana:
I deliver this statement on behalf of the African members of the Security Council, namely Algeria, Sierra Leone, and Somalia, as well as my own country, Guyana (A3+).

The A3+ welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution, which renews the sanctions regime established pursuant to resolution 2140 (2014) and extends the mandate of the Panel of Experts for an additional year. We express our appreciation to the penholder, the United Kingdom, for its constructive, balanced, and consultative approach throughout the negotiation process, which enabled the Council to maintain its unity on this important file.

The A3+ attaches great importance to the targeted sanctions measures and the work of the 2140 Sanctions Committee and its Panel of Experts as essential instruments to deter actions that threaten the peace, security, and stability of Yemen. We reaffirm our unwavering commitment to the unity, sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of Yemen.

We reiterate that there is no military solution to the conflict in Yemen. The only viable path forward is an inclusive, Yemeni-led and Yemeni-owned political process under the auspices of the United Nations. In this regard, we reaffirm our full support for the Special Envoy of the Secretary-General for Yemen, Mr. Hans Grundberg, and urge all Yemeni parties to engage constructively and without preconditions to finalize and implement an agreed political roadmap to end the conflict.

The A3+ remains deeply concerned by the dire humanitarian crisis and economic distress confronting millions of Yemeni civilians. We emphasize that sanctions measures must not impede humanitarian assistance or commercial imports of essential goods, and we call on the international community to scale up humanitarian funding and support for Yemen’s economic recovery. Furthermore, we demand the immediate, safe, and unconditional release of all detained United Nations, non-governmental organisation, and diplomatic personnel.

We also reaffirm the vital importance of maritime security and the preservation of navigational rights and freedoms in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, in accordance with international law, and stress the necessity of upholding the targeted arms embargo.

Finally, the A3+ welcomes recent de-escalatory steps in the wider region and emphasizes that a sustainable and comprehensive peace in Yemen is intrinsically linked to broader regional stability. We urge all parties to exercise maximum restraint, refrain from any provocative actions, and seize this opportunity to advance the political transition and bring lasting peace and prosperity to the people of Yemen.

I thank you.
after.Republic of Korea:
The Republic of Korea voted in favour of the resolution today, and we wish to express our gratitude to the penholder, the United Kingdom, for its dedicated efforts in facilitating this unanimous adoption renewing the Yemen sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts.

Today’s unanimous vote reaffirms the Security Council’s united commitment to supporting peace, stability, and security in Yemen and the wider region. As the latest report of the Panel of Experts (S/2025/650) demonstrates, the continuous illicit transfer of advanced weapons and military materiel into Yemen in violation of the targeted arms embargo remains a grave threat that fuels conflict and undermines regional stability. Such violations, alongside persistent threats to maritime security and commercial shipping in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, cannot be tolerated.

The Republic of Korea also remains deeply concerned by the ongoing arbitrary detention of United Nations, humanitarian, and diplomatic personnel by the Houthis. We reiterate our demand for their immediate, safe, and unconditional release. Furthermore, we call upon all parties to ensure safe, rapid, and unhindered humanitarian access to all civilians in need across Yemen.

There is no military solution to the conflict in Yemen. We reiterate our steadfast support for the Special Envoy of the Secretary-General in his pursuit of an inclusive, Yemeni-led and Yemeni-owned political process under UN auspices. 

Finally, as the Chair of the 2140 Sanctions Committee, the Republic of Korea calls upon all Member States to faithfully implement the sanctions measures and fully cooperate with the Committee and the Panel of Experts as they carry out their critical mandate.

I thank you.
after.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the United Kingdom extending the targeted sanctions measures on Yemen and the mandate of the Panel of Experts of the 2140 Sanctions Committee. 

Our support was guided by the importance of preserving the Security Council’s unity on the Yemeni track, especially against the backdrop of dangerous and ongoing regional turbulence. A balanced rollover of the existing sanctions architecture remains the most constructive way to support United Nations-led mediation efforts aimed at achieving a lasting political settlement among all Yemeni political forces.

At the same time, we deem it necessary to reiterate that Security Council sanctions must remain a targeted and auxiliary instrument in service of the political process, rather than a punitive tool used to exert pressure on inconvenient political actors or to aggravate divisions within the country and across the region. 

We once again firmly reject any attempts to interpret Security Council resolutions expansively or arbitrarily. Council decisions provide no legal basis for conducting unauthorized maritime interdictions or inspections of commercial vessels on the high seas, let alone for diverting seized military goods to third countries for subsequent use in other conflicts. Furthermore, we reiterate our position that unlawful military strikes carried out against targets inside Yemeni territory by Western coalitions not only violate the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Yemen, but also fail to resolve security challenges, serving only to heighten tensions and jeopardize the prospects for a comprehensive intra-Yemeni peace process.

Russia remains convinced that there is no military solution to the conflict in Yemen. We will continue our constructive engagement with all Yemeni sides and regional partners to facilitate dialogue and help restore lasting peace and stability to Yemen.
after.Somalia:
Mr. President,

Somalia welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution renewing the targeted sanctions regime on Yemen and extending the mandate of the Panel of Experts. We thank the United Kingdom, the penholder, for its constructive engagement and dedication throughout the negotiation process.

Somalia voted in favour of this resolution because we firmly believe that the targeted sanctions measures and the vital work of the Panel of Experts remain indispensable tools for supporting peace, stability, and security in Yemen and the wider region. As a close maritime neighbour sharing the waters of the Gulf of Aden and the Red Sea, Somalia’s security and stability are deeply intertwined with that of Yemen. 

We particularly welcome the resolution’s emphasis on addressing the illicit flow and transfer of arms and weapons. The nexus between illicit maritime trafficking networks across the Gulf of Aden and regional terrorist organisations, including Al-Shabaab and Al-Qaida in the Arabian Peninsula, presents a grave and persistent threat to our collective peace and security. In this regard, we strongly support the mandate directing enhanced cooperation between the Panel of Experts on Yemen and the Panel of Experts on Somalia. Disrupting these illicit supply chains and strengthening maritime security are essential to curbing terrorist financing and weapons proliferation.

Somalia reaffirms its unwavering commitment to the unity, sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of Yemen. We reiterate our support for the efforts of the Special Envoy of the Secretary-General to facilitate an inclusive, Yemeni-led and Yemeni-owned political settlement. There is no military solution to this conflict; only sustained dialogue, de-escalation, and genuine commitment to peace can alleviate the profound suffering of the brotherly Yemeni people.

Finally, we express our grave concern over the humanitarian situation in Yemen and the ongoing detention of United Nations and humanitarian personnel, and we call for their immediate, safe, and unconditional release. Somalia stands ready to continue working constructively with all members of the Council and regional partners to achieve lasting peace and stability in Yemen and our shared maritime domain.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution renewing the Yemen sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts for a further twelve months. We thank all Council colleagues for their constructive engagement throughout negotiations.

By adopting this resolution today, the Security Council has sent a clear and united message: the targeted sanctions measures remain a vital tool to constrain destabilising activities in Yemen, deter the illicit flow of weapons in violation of the targeted arms embargo, and support efforts toward sustainable peace and security. The independent reporting and monitoring of the Panel of Experts is indispensable to the Council’s work, and we urge all parties and Member States to cooperate fully with the Panel.

We remain deeply concerned by the Houthis’ ongoing threats to regional stability, including their attacks on commercial and merchant shipping in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, which jeopardize maritime security and international navigation. We also reiterate our grave concern over the arbitrary detention by the Houthis of United Nations, NGO, and diplomatic personnel, and we once again demand their immediate and unconditional release.

The United Kingdom reaffirms its steadfast commitment to the unity, sovereignty, and territorial integrity of Yemen. There is no military solution to this conflict. We reaffirm our full support for the Special Envoy of the Secretary-General, Hans Grundberg, in his tireless efforts to advance an inclusive, Yemeni-led and Yemeni-owned political process under United Nations auspices, and we call on all parties to prioritize dialogue and the welfare of the Yemeni people.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President.

The United States welcomes the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution, renewing the Yemen sanctions regime and extending the mandate of the Panel of Experts. We thank the United Kingdom for its leadership as penholder on this critical file.

Today’s vote sends a clear and united message: the international community remains resolved in countering the threats to peace, security, and stability in Yemen and the wider region. The targeted sanctions regime established under Resolution 2140, together with the targeted arms embargo under Resolution 2216, remains an indispensable tool to constrain the destabilizing activities of the Houthis and disrupt the illicit flow of weapons and material that fuel conflict.

The Panel of Experts plays an essential role in documenting violations of the arms embargo and exposing the illicit procurement networks that sustain Houthi aggression. For years, Iran has continued to transfer advanced conventional weapons, ballistic missiles, and unmanned aerial systems to the Houthis in flagrant violation of Security Council resolutions. These illicit weapons transfers have directly enabled the Houthis’ reckless and unlawful attacks against commercial vessels in the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, endangering innocent mariners, disrupting vital global trade, and threatening regional navigation. All Member States must faithfully implement their obligations under Council resolutions to cut off these weapons supply lines.

The United States also reiterates its vehement condemnation of the Houthis’ ongoing arbitrary detention of United Nations personnel, staff of international and non-governmental organizations, and diplomatic personnel, including locally employed staff of the former U.S. Embassy in Sana’a. These brazen and unlawful detentions severely undermine humanitarian operations at a time when millions of Yemenis are in desperate need of lifesaving assistance. We demand the immediate, safe, and unconditional release of all detained personnel.

Finally, the United States reaffirms its steadfast commitment to an inclusive, Yemeni-led and Yemeni-owned political resolution to the conflict under United Nations auspices, in support of Special Envoy Grundberg. Only a credible political settlement can bring long-term peace, security, and relief to the people of Yemen. 

Thank you, Mr. President.
